Constipation in cats can sometimes be more than just a temporary digestive problem. Megacolon is a serious condition where the colon becomes enlarged and loses its ability to function properly, leading to chronic constipation and discomfort.

At The Progressive Pet Clinic, we’ve shared a detailed article to help pet parents recognize the early signs including straining, infrequent bowel movements, loss of appetite, and lethargy and understand available treatment options, from dietary management to advanced medical care.

Time for a Summer Cut for pets

A summer cut for pets especially dogs and long-haired cats is all about keeping them cool, clean, and comfortable during hot weather. But it’s not just about shaving everything off the right approach depends a lot on your pet’s breed and coat type.

Common symptoms include fever,  lethargy , vomiting,  and weakness.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Hello,
I am extremely disappointed and angry with the kind of service provided at your hospital.
I had clearly informed the doctor that the animal I brought was not my personal pet, but a building kitten, one of six kittens left behind after the owners shifted. Despite this important background, the doctor showed zero effort to understand the situation, history, or real condition of the animal.
The consultation was completely directionless:
No clear understanding of the problem
No explanation of what happened, why it happened, or how to handle it
No meaningful guidance or responsibility shown
Yet, fees were taken without hesitation.
If a doctor cannot even understand the basic context of the case and cannot explain the issue in simple terms, then on what basis are you charging money? This is professional negligence, not consultation.
Animal care is not a joke or a money-collection exercise. People bring animals in distress expecting knowledge, clarity, and accountability — none of which were provided.
I expect this complaint to be taken seriously and the matter to be reviewed internally. Such behaviour reflects very poorly on your hospital and discourages people from helping stray or abandoned animals.

We are genuinely sorry to hear that you left our clinic feeling disappointed. We take such feedback seriously and shall surely perform an internal audit to reassess the situation. 

We understand your concern, especially when it involves a vulnerable abandoned kitten, and we appreciate that you took the effort to seek medical help for the animal. This shows you are a responsible and understanding individual. 

At our clinic, every patient — whether a personal pet, rescued stray, or community animal — is treated with care and medical attention to the best of our ability. Veterinary consultations are based on the clinical condition of the patient presented at that moment, especially in cases where prior medical history may not be available. 

That said, we regret if the communication during the consultation did not meet your expectations or if you felt your concerns were not adequately addressed. We shall work harder to deliver information and clarity in future. 

We agree that clarity and guidance are an important part of veterinary care, and your feedback will be discussed internally with the team to improve the experience for caregivers and rescuers alike in future.

We would also like to respectfully mention that consultations involve the doctor’s professional time, clinical assessment, and medical judgement, irrespective of whether the animal is owned, rescued, or community-fed. However, we always strive to ensure that pet parents and rescuers leave with a better understanding of the condition and next steps.

We sincerely appreciate people who step forward to help abandoned and stray animals, and we hope this experience does not discourage you from continuing to do so.


Please feel free to connect with us if youd like more clarity on the patient. We are happy to discuss the radiographs and the reports. 

Anything in the interest of the patient. 

Wishing the kitten a safe recovery and good health ahead.

featured_reviews.name: vikas nalawade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review about a stray cat named “Leopard” who eventually became our family member. Request you to please read it till end, as it may be helpful to any pet parent.
Leopard met with an accident and was missing for a week’s period. Later we found him & we noticed that he had a fracture at shoulder of right forelimb. Doctors told us that leg needs to be operated by inserting rod in his leg, so we got him operated by Dr. Sunetra. The surgery went well, but three days after surgery, Leopard's operated leg started swelling, we informed Dr. Sunetra but she told us it is the swelling due to surgery and it will subside downwards. But that swelling was due to infection and it lead to pus formation. Next day the swelling increased and in the evening pus started oozing out, seeing this we called up Dr. Sunetra & rushed to her with our Leopard. Dr. told us to keep flushing the wound twice a day with betadine. After 2-3 days of this treatment, the skin around the infected area went dead and we had a clear sight of his wound with operated area, where we could see his bone from two points because healing was not completed & the stitches were opened. We even asked Dr. Sunetra the doubt in our mind that this infection will not spread in his operated leg & internal body, to which she responded, it would not.
Eventually his external pain reduced but he had internal pain, which we failed to understand. He could not tolerate the pain and stopped eating and got fever exactly on 8th day from operation. We informed this situation of Leopard at every visit to Dr. Sunetra, but she recommended to force feed our Leopard. Later on our Leopard left with no energy to walk on his own and lift his neck, he even started heavy breathing. After informing this situation to Dr. Sunetra, she then advised us to put saline for his recovery but nowhere had she conveyed that Leopard’s health is deteriorating & he needs hospitalization. At this time, she was going out of town & was not available for 4-5 days.
Since, Dr. Sunetra was not available, we went to other Vet doctor who knew Leopard's medical history. This doctor told us to continue saline treatment twice a day for at least 4-5 days. Here the blood test was also done to examine the condition of our Leopard, where the report came with alarming & critical output depicting WBC increased & Platelets dropped to severe condition. Even this doctor also not recommended that our Leopard require hospitalization. This was the 11th day after operation.
The 12th day story (i.e. 1st July 23) of our Leopard was worst. The morning session of his saline was completed & even this second doctor went out of town for 3-4 days without recommending hospitalization. By evening, somewhere from 4:30pm, the heavy breathing became worse & we could not see his pain. We started calling Dr. Sunetra, but her phone was not reachable, so we text her on WhatsApp along with Leopard’s blood report. Since no response from doctor, with Leopard, we rushed to a Vet hospital, where he was admitted with a note by the doctors, like heavy breathing & drop in body temperature, which was very critical condition. He was kept in ICU incubator with oxygen supply to ease his breathe & improve his body temperature. The hospital doctors even told us that there are chances that the infection might have spread into blood. Unfortunately battling with pain & breathing problem our Leopard passed away on the same day around 11 pm.
There are certain questions for Dr. Sunetra;
# Why you haven't included any medicine for infection post-surgery?
# Why you did not advised us prior to start saline, when we informed you that Leopard lost his appetite?
# Why you did not look closely if the infection was spreading in the body? If you think it wasn't then why did he lost his appetite, had weakness, got fever, started heavy breathing?
# Why you took everything so lightly and casually in his case? Was it because it was a stray cat?

The doctor’s entire focus was on the operated area and the wound & the rest health parameters were ignored completely.

What a “wonderful” experience it was to lose my cat within 24 hours of visiting this so-called doctor. My poor cat was so sick, and instead of honesty or care, all I got was a handful of medicines worth ₹5000 and a cheerful instruction to “come daily for fluids.”

Of course, no mention that my cat’s condition was critical  because why tell the truth when there’s money to be made? 💔

It’s heartbreaking and infuriating that someone who claims to heal animals can be so careless and insensitive. My pet deserved compassion, not a business transaction.

Please, don’t make the mistake I did. Keep your pets far away from this clinic  they deserve real care, not fake promises wrapped in medical coats.
